claims.text: The alloy (W1.5Ni2.25Fe)95Ta5 has a dual-phase BCC/FCC structure.
The as-cast alloy has a yield strength of approximately 600 MPa.
The initial alloy has limited ductility because of its coarse microstructure and lack of coherent strengthening phases.

The processing route consists of hot rolling at 1200 °C with 80% reduction, cold rolling at 25 °C with 75% reduction, annealing at 900 °C for 5 min, and aging at 650 °C for 20 h followed by water quenching.
The stepwise route produces two distinct coherent precipitate populations: δ lamellae and γ″ particles.
The dual coherent precipitate population simultaneously enhances yield strength and tensile ductility, overcoming the conventional trade-off.
The δ lamellae are approximately 40 nm wide and the γ″ particles are approximately 10 nm in size.
The δ precipitates have a D0a structure and the γ″ precipitates have a D022 structure.
The δ-lamellar boundaries hinder dislocation motion.
Slip bands shear the δ lamellae and cause coherent misalignment rather than cracking.
The γ″ particles strengthen the alloy through order hardening and lattice-misfit strengthening.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission, relieve stress concentrations, prevent premature crack initiation, and maintain high strain-hardening rates.
The processed alloy reaches a yield strength of approximately 2.0 GPa at room temperature.
The processed alloy reaches an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 2.15 GPa at room temperature.
The processed alloy reaches approximately 15% tensile elongation at room temperature.
The processed alloy retains high strength at 800 °C.
The stepwise-processed alloy surpasses both the as-cast baseline and standard single-phase thermal treatments.
Simple aging or homogenization typically produces coarse incoherent precipitates or single-phase microstructures that show either high strength with low ductility or high ductility with low strength.

The strategy applies to refractory high-entropy alloys with dual BCC/FCC structures capable of forming coherent D0a and D022 precipitates, but may fail with incoherent precipitates or unsuitable matrix stacking-fault energy.
Aging above 800 °C can be used to induce incoherent precipitates in this alloy.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that a standard or single-step treatment will retain the conventional high-strength/low-ductility trade-off, yet the falsification rule says observing yield strength above 1.5 GPa with ductility below 5% in that control would falsify the coherent-precipitation hypothesis. That control result would instead be consistent with the stated baseline and would not falsify the stepwise sample's proposed advantage.
